clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive hypomyelinating leukodystrophy (type HLD3) caused by variants in AIMP1, encoding a scaffold protein of the multi-tRNA synthetase complex
It is a severe, early-onset disorder typically presenting in the first months of life with profound developmental delay or regression
Common features include acquired microcephaly, early and often refractory seizures, spasticity, and later contractures, with many children failing to attain significant motor milestones
MRI shows diffuse hypomyelination, and with time superimposed cerebral atrophy develops as the disease advances
The severity and early onset help distinguish it from milder hypomyelinating leukodystrophies, though genetic confirmation is required
Diagnosis rests on recognition of a severe infantile hypomyelinating pattern on MRI with AIMP1 sequencing, usually after commoner causes such as PLP1 have been considered
There is no specific treatment; care is supportive and multidisciplinary, with seizure control, spasticity and contracture management, nutrition and family support
reference.pathophysiology: AIMP1-related leukodystrophy is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in AIMP1, which encodes an auxiliary protein (also known as p43) that scaffolds and stabilises the multi-enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase complex central to protein synthesis. Loss of AIMP1 destabilises this complex and may also disturb additional functions attributed to the protein in cytoskeletal and neuronal regulation. The resulting impairment of protein synthesis and cellular homeostasis affects oligodendrocytes and neurons during a critical developmental window, producing failure of myelination (hypomyelination) alongside progressive neuronal loss and cerebral atrophy, which together account for the severe early-onset encephalopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Severe infantile epileptic encephalopathies with white matter involvement
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to demonstrate diffuse hypomyelination and any evolving cerebral atrophy
AIMP1 sequencing, with a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy panel or exome if targeted testing is negative
PLP1 analysis to exclude the commonest cause of infantile hypomyelination
Electroencephalography to characterise the seizure disorder
Metabolic screen to exclude treatable causes of an infantile encephalopathy
Developmental, feeding and physiotherapy assessment to guide supportive care
redFlags: Refractory seizures or status epilepticus requiring intensive management
Severe feeding difficulty with aspiration and faltering growth
Respiratory compromise from bulbar and truncal involvement
reference.prognosis: AIMP1-related leukodystrophy is a severe, progressive disorder with early onset; affected children commonly have profound neurodevelopmental impairment, refractory epilepsy and marked motor disability, and life expectancy is significantly reduced in the most severe cases. Care is directed at comfort, seizure control and support for the child and family.
pitfalls: Stopping the genetic workup after a negative PLP1 result and missing AIMP1-related disease
Interpreting hypomyelination as delayed myelination without appropriate follow-up imaging
Attributing the picture to hypoxic-ischaemic injury or non-specific developmental delay
Underestimating the seizure burden and its impact on the child and family
Omitting autosomal recessive genetic counselling and recurrence-risk discussion
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: No disease-modifying therapy exists; care centres on symptom control and comfort for this severe infantile encephalopathy
Anticonvulsant therapy for the early, often refractory epilepsy, selecting agents by seizure type
Spasticity management with antispasticity agents such as baclofen alongside physiotherapy and orthoses to limit contractures
Feeding and nutritional support with speech-and-language swallow assessment and gastrostomy for unsafe swallow or failure to thrive
Surveillance for aspiration, recurrent respiratory infection and nutritional decline
Multidisciplinary neurodisability care with early paediatric palliative involvement
Genetic counselling for parents given autosomal recessive inheritance, with carrier and prenatal testing for future pregnancies
